questions.question: The total of three numbers is 240. The second number is four times the first number. The third number is three times the first number. What will be the average of the three numbers?
questions.questionHtml: The total of three numbers is 240. The second number is four times the first number. The third number is three times the first number. What will be the average of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
Let the numbers is x, y and z.

Given :-

The total of three numbers is 240

So, x + y + z = 240 → eq. (i)

The second number is four times the first number.

y = 4x

The third number is three times the first number.

z = 3x

Put the value of y and z in eq. (i)

x + 4x + 3x = 240

8x = 240

x = 30

So,

Second number is y = 4x = 4 × 30 = 120

Third number is z = 3x = 3 × 30 = 90

Average of numbers = Sum of total number ÷ total numbers

(30 + 120 + 90) ÷ 3 = 240 ÷ 3 = 80

Hence, average of that three number is ‘80’

 Shortcut Trick

Average of numbers = Sum of total number ÷ total numbers

Sum of total number is given 240

So,

Average of numbers = 240 ÷ 3 = 80

Hence, average of that three number is ‘80’.

questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation.

14 * 7 * 39 * 133 * 19 * 130
questions.solution:
According to BODMAS rule

Given equation 14 * 7 * 39 * 133 * 19 * 130

Option 1 : Using the combination ÷, +, -, ×, =

14 ÷ 7 + 39 - 133 × 19 = 130

By BODMAS rule

2 + 39 – 133 × 19 = 130

2 + 39 – 2527 = 130

41 – 2527 = 130

-2486 = 130 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 2 : Using combination ×, -, +, ÷, =

14 × 7 - 39 + 133 ÷ 19 = 130

14 × 7 - 39 + 7 = 130

98 - 39 + 7 = 130

105 – 39 = 130

66 = 130 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 3 : Using the combination ×, +, -, ÷, =

14 × 7 + 39 - 133 ÷ 19 = 130

14 × 7 + 39 - 7 = 130

98 + 39 – 7 = 130

137 – 7 = 130

130 = 130 (LHS = RHS)

Option 4 : Using the combination ÷, -, +, ×, =

14 ÷ 7 - 39 + 133 × 19 = 130

2 - 39 + 133 × 19 = 130

2 - 39 + 2527 = 130

2529 - 39 = 130

2490 = 130 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Hence, the answer is “×, +, -, ÷, =”.

questions.question: In which of the following years did Japan invade India resulting in the Battle of Imphal?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following years did Japan invade India resulting in the Battle of Imphal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1944.

  • In 1944, Japan invade India resulting in the Battle of Imphal.

Key Points

  • The Battle of Imphal took place from March to July 1944 in the vicinity of the city of Imphal, the capital of the state of Manipur in northeastern India.
    • Japanese forces attempted to destroy the Allied forces at Imphal and invade India, but were driven back to Burma with heavy losses.
    • Together with the Battle of Kohima on the road, by which the Allied forces at Imphal were relieved, the battle was the turning point of the Burma Campaign, which was part of the South-East Asian Theater of World War II.
    • The defeats at Kohima and Imphal were the largest defeats to date in Japanese history, with many Japanese deaths from hunger, disease and exhaustion during their retreat.

Additional Information

  • The operation to take Imphal was named U-go by the Japanese Army.
  • It consisted of elements from the 31st Infantry Division of the Japanese Army and as well as units from the Indian National Army, who were in primarily support and scouting roles.
  • The Japanese Army crossed into India on the night of 7th March and engaged the British Indian forces guarding the frontiers the morning of 8th March 1944.

The correct answer is The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.

Key Points

  • The net magnetic flux through any closed surface will be zero.

Additional Information

  • Gauss' Law for Magnetism:
    • Gauss' Law for magnetism applies to the magnetic flux through a closed surface. In this case, the area vector points out from the surface.
    • Because magnetic field lines are continuous loops, all closed surfaces have as many magnetic field lines going in as coming out. Hence, the net magnetic flux through a closed surface is zero.
    • Net flux = ∫ B • dA = 0
    • Gauss' Law for charges was a very useful method for calculating electric fields in highly symmetric situations.
    • Gauss' Law for magnetism is considerably less useful, but we'll come up with another law that enables us to calculate magnetic fields in highly symmetric situations. 

Magnetic flux:

  • Magnetic flux is defined as the number of magnetic field lines passing through a given closed surface.
  • It provides the measurement of the total magnetic field that passes through a given surface area.
  • It is a scalar quantity.
  • The SI unit of magnetic flux is Weber (Wb).

​Magnetic flux associated with any area is given as,

⇒ ϕB = BAcosθ

Where ϕB = magnetic flux, B = magnetic field intensity, A = area, and θ = angle between B and A

questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle in minor segment with center O. C is a point on the minor arc of the circle between the points A and B. The tangents to the circle at A and B meet at the point P. If ∠ACB = 102°, then what is the measure of ∠APB?
questions.questionHtml: AB is a chord of a circle in minor segment with center O. C is a point on the minor arc of the circle between the points A and B. The tangents to the circle at A and B meet at the point P. If ∠ACB = 102°, then what is the measure of ∠APB?
questions.solution:
Given:

∠ACB = 102°

Concept Used:

When a quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle, the opposite angles of it are supplementary angles.

The angle subtended at the center is always double the angle subtended at the remaining arc.

The radius from the center of the circle to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

Calculation:

Point D is taken on the major arc of the circle. Then, A & D, B & D, C & B, and A & C are joined.

∠ACB = 102°

Now,

∠ADB = (180 – 102)° = 78°

Now,

∠AOB = (78 × 2)° = 156°

Since OA = OB, ΔAOB is an isosceles triangle and ∠OBA = ∠OAB.

Now,

∠AOB + ∠OBA + ∠OAB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OBA = (180 – 156)°

⇒ ∠OBA = 12°

Now,

∠OBA = 12°

∠OAB = 12°

Now,

∠OAP = ∠OAB + ∠BAP

⇒ 90° = 12° + ∠BAP

⇒ ∠BAP = 78°

Now,

∠OBP = ∠OBA + ∠ABP

⇒ 90° = 12° + ∠ABP

⇒ ∠ABP = 78°

Now,

∠APB + ∠ABP + ∠BAP = 180°

⇒ ∠APB + 78° + 78° = 180°

⇒ ∠APB = 180° - (2 × 78)°

⇒ ∠APB = 24°

∴ The required measure of ∠APB is 24°.

Percentage calculation

Calculation:

Marked price

⇒ P (1 + 0.25)

⇒ (P × 1.25)

After 10% discount

⇒ (P × 1.125) × 0.95

⇒ (P × 1.06875)

According to the question,

(P × 1.06875) = 2394

⇒ P = 2394 ÷ 1.06875

⇒ P = 2240

∴ The cost price of the item purchased by Shruti is Rs. 2240.

questions.question: In an examination, 45% of all the students who appeared are boys and the rest are girls. If 60% of the boys and 70% of the girls passed, then what is the percentage of students who failed?
questions.questionHtml: In an examination, 45% of all the students who appeared are boys and the rest are girls. If 60% of the boys and 70% of the girls passed, then what is the percentage of students who failed?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the total number of students in the examination be 100.

Number of boys = 45, which means number of girls = 55.

Boys who failed = (100 − 60)% of 45 = 40% of 45 = 18.

Girls who failed = (100 − 70)% of 55 = 30% of 55 = 16.5.

Total failed percentage = 18 + 16.5 = 34.5%.

∴ The correct answer is 34.5%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total students considered = 100%

Percentage of boys = 45%

Passed boys = 60%

Passed girls = 70%

Formula Used:

Failed % = 100% − Passed %

Calculations:

⇒ Percentage of girls = 100% − 45% = 55%

⇒ Number of boys failed out of 100 = 40% of 45 = (40 ÷ 100) × 45 = 18

⇒ Number of girls failed out of 100 = 30% of 55 = (30 ÷ 100) × 55 = 16.5

⇒ Total failed students = 18 + 16.5 = 34.5

⇒ Percentage of students who failed = (34.5 ÷ 100) × 100% = 34.5%

∴ The correct answer is 34.5%.

Additional Information

Percentage Change

Percentage change is calculated as ((New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value) × 100.

Successive Percentage

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by (a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100)%.

Base Shift Rule

If A is R% more than B, then B is (R ÷ (100 + R)) × 100% less than A.

questions.question: What is the difference (in Rs.) between the simple interest and the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 8000 for \(2\frac{2}{5}\) years at the rate of 10% p.a. when the interest is compounded yearly?
questions.questionHtml: What is the difference (in Rs.) between the simple interest and the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 8000 for \(2\frac{2}{5}\) years at the rate of 10% p.a. when the interest is compounded yearly?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net Simple Interest (SI) rate for 2.4 years at 10% = 10% × 2.4 = 24%.

Successive rates for Compound Interest (CI): 10%, 10%, and (10 × 2/5)% = 4%.

Net CI rate = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%; then 21 + 4 + (21 × 4)/100 = 25.84%.

Difference in percentage = 25.84% − 24% = 1.84%.

Difference in value = 1.84% of ₹8000 = 80 × 1.84 = ₹147.20.

∴ The correct answer is ₹147.20.

Alternate Method

Given: Principal (P) = ₹8000, Rate (R) = 10% p.a., Time (T) = 22/5 years = 2.4 years.

Formula Used: SI = (P × R × T) / 100 | CI Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)n

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) = (8000 × 10 × 2.4) / 100

⇒ SI = 80 × 24 = ₹1920

⇒ Compound Interest Amount (A) = 8000 × (1 + 10/100) × (1 + 10/100) × (1 + 4/100)

⇒ A = 8000 × 1.1 × 1.1 × 1.04

⇒ A = 8000 × 1.21 × 1.04 = 9680 × 1.04 = ₹10067.20

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = 10067.20 − 8000 = ₹2067.20

⇒ Difference = 2067.20 − 1920 = ₹147.20

∴ The correct answer is ₹147.20.

Additional Information

CI and SI Difference (2 Years)

For a period of 2 years, the difference is calculated as: Diff = P(R/100)2.

CI and SI Difference (3 Years)

For a period of 3 years, the difference is: Diff = P(R/100)2 × (3 + R/100).

Fractional Time Period CI

If time is T = n + a/b years, Amount = P(1 + R/100)n × (1 + (a/b × R)/100).

Concept used:

x4 + y4 + x2y2 = (x2 + y2 - xy)(x2 + y2 + xy)

Calculation:

Given that, 

x4 + y4 + x2y2 = 21   -----(1)

x2 + y2 - xy = 7         -----(2)

We know that,

x4 + y4 + x2y2 = (x2 + y2 - xy)(x2 + y2 + xy)

Using equation (1) & (2)

⇒ 21 = 7(x2 + y2 + xy)

⇒ (x2 + y2 + xy) = 3      ----(3)

Now.

(x2 + y2 + xy) + (x2 + y2 - xy) = 3 + 7

⇒ x2 + y2 = 5

Put this value in equation (3)

⇒ 5 + xy = 3

⇒ xy = - 2

Now, \(\frac{x}{y}+\frac{y}{x} = \frac{ x^2 + y^2}{xy}\)

⇒ ​\(\frac{x}{y}+\frac{y}{x}\)​  = - 5/2

∴ The required answer is - 5/2

questions.questionHtml: Chord AB of a circle of radius 10 cm is at a distance 8 cm from the centre O. If tangents drawn at A and B intersect at P., then the length of the tangent AP (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In right-angled ▵OMA, AM = √(102 − 82) = 6 cm.

In ▵OAP, using the property of similarity (or altitude in a right triangle):

AP/OA = AM/OM

⇒ AP/10 = 6/8

⇒ AP = 60/8 = 7.5 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 7.5 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: Radius (OA) = 10 cm, distance from centre (OM) = 8 cm.

Formula Used: In a right-angled triangle, the tangent is perpendicular to the radius. Pythagoras Theorem: H2 = P2 + B2.

In ▵OMA, ∠OMA = 90° (Perpendicular from centre to chord).

⇒ AM2 = OA2 − OM2

⇒ AM2 = 102 − 82 = 100 − 64 = 36

⇒ AM = 6 cm.

In right-angled ▵OAP, AM is the altitude to the hypotenuse OP (as OP bisects AB perpendicularly).

From similarity of ▵OMA and ▵AMP (or properties of right triangles):

⇒ AM/OM = AP/OA

⇒ 6 / 8 = AP / 10

⇒ AP = (6 × 10) ÷ 8

⇒ AP = 60 ÷ 8 = 7.5 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 7.5 cm.

Additional Information

Tangent-Radius Property

A tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact (∠OAP = 90°).

Right Triangle Proportionality

In ▵OAP with altitude AM, the legs and altitude satisfy: OA2 = OM × OP and AP2 = PM × PO.

Chord Bisection

The line joining the external point P and the centre O is the perpendicular bisector of the chord of contact AB.

questions.question: The perimeter of a semi circle is 25.7 cm. What is its diameter (in cm)? (π = 3.14)
questions.questionHtml: The perimeter of a semi circle is 25.7 cm. What is its diameter (in cm)? (π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Perimeter of a semi-circle = r(π + 2)

Given π = 3.14, Perimeter = r(3.14 + 2) = 5.14r

5.14r = 25.7 ⇒ r = 25.7 ÷ 5.14 = 5 cm

Diameter = 2 × r = 2 × 5 = 10 cm

∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: Perimeter of semi-circle = 25.7 cm, π = 3.14

Formula Used: Perimeter = πr + 2r

⇒ r(π + 2) = 25.7

⇒ r(3.14 + 2) = 25.7

⇒ 5.14r = 25.7

⇒ r = 25.7 ÷ 5.14

⇒ r = 5 cm

⇒ Diameter = 2r = 2 × 5 = 10 cm

∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.

Additional Information

Area of a Semi-circle

The area is half the area of a full circle: Area = (πr2) ÷ 2.

Circle Properties

For a full circle, Circumference = 2πr and Diameter = 2r.

Sector of a Circle

Perimeter of a sector with angle θ = ( θ / 360 ) × 2πr + 2r.
